title: Make composition obligatory
played: Required policy sections enter each mechanism.
alternative: Keep optional numbers and local fallback defaults.
stake: A missing policy input becomes a missing constructor argument; clocks, storage, paths and worker injection remain separate dependencies.
reason: The PR says omitted composition must not recreate local defaults.

title: Use the resource snapshot verbatim
played: Supervisor, ready record and worker heap use policy.resources.
alternative: Re-derive resources from effective memory or a separate memory cap.
stake: The hard cap reported at readiness and the worker heap limit now come from the same supplied values. The CLI resource-policy class is deleted.
reason: The policy record requires one complete snapshot across process and worker boundaries; the architecture spec gives thresholds one owner.

title: Carry the output limits all the way through
played: Capture, spool, disk decode and both worker endpoints share output limits.
alternative: Give each output stage its own constants and optional capacities.
stake: A record accepted by one stage is checked against the same chunk limit at later stages. Local CLI execution also consumes the output section.
reason: The PR explicitly routes output capture, spooling and worker validation through required output slices; the record states why each bound exists.
reason_source: PR · Shape; policy record · output rows
scope: 64 KiB raw chunks → 256 KiB inline → 256 MiB per result → 512 MiB aggregate spool. These are existing defaults, not new tuning.

title: Keep three framing capacities distinct
played: Ordinary JSON, execution control and raw binary chunks keep separate bounds.
alternative: Use one frame-size limit for all traffic.
stake: The transfer decoder allows a binary envelope of control capacity plus chunk capacity; the codec separately checks raw chunk length. Socket write fragmentation remains an option.
reason: The policy record distinguishes decoded control input, binary-transfer control and one raw record.
reason_source: Policy record · transport and output rows

variation: Control size and raw data size become coupled

title: Choose the timeout by caller purpose
played: Status observer: 100 ms. Ordinary transport: 250 ms.
alternative: Choose a timeout from the request’s kind.
stake: The same identify or ping message can serve different callers. An execution-status request still uses the ordinary timeout; the word “status” does not select 100 ms.
reason: The PR says status observation and ordinary execution-status requests have distinct deadlines.
reason_source: PR · Decisions, second item
scope: The CLI status action sets responseTimeoutPurpose: status-observer. Ordinary is the default purpose. The constructor selects the value once.
question: Is the timeout a property of the message, or of the job the caller is doing?

title: End the execution timer at acceptance
played: Policy supplies the 5 s admission timer; acceptance disables it.
alternative: Carry that timer into command completion.
stake: Long accepted work keeps running without a completion deadline. Fetch and worker-output acknowledgement also retain their existing absence of a timer.
reason: The policy record bounds admission without timing accepted completion; accepted work must not be replayed or failed for running long.
reason_source: Policy record · admission row and intentional absences
scope: This is preserved behavior while the timer’s source changes. Healthy startup and unacknowledged-result retention likewise have no new expiry.
variation: Long accepted work reaches that deadline
question: Which event changes the client’s obligation from “submit” to “wait for accepted work”?

title: Give recovery two independent budgets
played: Count execute reattachments outside; count fetch resumes inside each execute attempt.
alternative: Share a single used-retry flag across both recovery scopes.
stake: A reattached execute attempt receives a fresh fetch allowance. Reattachment resends the same request identity after an authenticated accepted close; this is recovery, not local replay.
reason: The PR says every reattached execute attempt has its own fetch-resume allowance.
reason_source: PR · Decisions, third item
scope: Default: one reattachment and one fetch resume per attempt. Base already nested the two scopes; this PR replaces fixed one-shot control with policy numbers. Added trace: execute → reattach → fetch.

Execute attempt B · fresh resume count

title: Let the latest completion error escape
played: A later accepted completion failure is caught in the next loop iteration.
alternative: Always preserve the original accepted-close error.
stake: When reattachment is accepted and its completion fails, the exposed error can now be that later failure. A failure before reattachment acceptance still rethrows the preceding error.
reason: No reason for this error-selection change was found in the PR, six commit messages, policy record or architecture spec.
reason_source: Unexplained · behavior detail not called out by PR

title: Keep the fetch path as one connection
played: Read a numeric resume allowance at the original execute socket; fetch itself has no retry loop.
alternative: Retry failed fetch connections until that numeric allowance is spent.
stake: The code distinguishes an allowance from a complete repeated-fetch mechanism. Fetch failure rejects this attempt. The new reattachment test makes one fetch; it does not demonstrate repeated fetch failures with a limit above one.
reason: The PR explains independent counters, but does not explain retaining one fetch connection while accepting a numeric resume limit.
reason_source: Unexplained · the larger-than-one fetch case
scope: Default limit is one. The limit check lives in executeOnce.resume(); fetchCompletion().catch(fail) exits the attempt. Outer recovery still has its own eligibility checks.

played: Use 15 s coordination grace for ownership; leave healthy readiness waiting unbounded.
alternative: Use “startup timeout” as one wall-clock deadline for every startup phase.
stake: Registry ownership, daemon authorization and missing-owner observation consume the grace. A progressing warm-up does not expire because a large project takes time.
reason: The policy record preserves election recovery grace and explicitly gives progressing warm-up no project-size deadline.

scope: The unused startupTimeoutMs field is removed; the active grace is named coordinationGraceMs. Grace still has a scalar override on a registry helper (move 21).

alternative: Use a hard-coded catch-and-try-once branch.
stake: Only child exit or lost warm-up consumes this recovery route. Waiting for another owner does not reset the budget. Default one retry is preserved; tests exercise zero and two.
